reproduction: python3 fedmuon_ogd/run_split_mnist.py --rounds 10 --local-steps 4 --lr 0.01 --lr-bias 0.01 --rank-per-task 2 --k-max 8 --soft-alpha 0.5 --seeds 0 1 --methods fedmuon proj feasible soft classrow --out fedmuon_ogd/outputs_directions

setting_in_same_file.partition: IID equal shard within each task

evaluation: evaluate_task keeps test rows whose label is in the task pair, then takes argmax over all 10 logits. Seen-class subset, not masked logits.

freezing_old_logits_does_not_fix_argmax.statement: Layer protection and freezing old head rows do not guarantee class-incremental accuracy. Old logits can stay fixed while a new-class logit changes the argmax.

compute: 4 CPU threads, torch 2.15.0+cpu, CUDA unavailable. No GPU was used.

fedmuon_bias_correction.matches_paper_update: M <- (1-alpha)M + alpha grad; step uses lmo(M - C_i + C); C_i <- M; full participation averages parameters and control increments by 1/n.
deviations: Newton-Schulz coefficients are the quintic 3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315, not FedMuon's 15/8, -5/4, 3/8.
No per-layer dimension rescaling of the step size.
Momentum and controls are reset at every task boundary.
The 56.3% method additionally zeros old output rows after the matrix sign and zeros old biases. That is not FedMuon.
Five Newton-Schulz steps, not an exact polar factor.
Data are IID equal shards and all 8 clients participate. FedMuon's reported experiments use Dirichlet partitions and partial participation.
